subject.title: [Feishu] "This reply completed without visible content" fallback incorrectly triggered for long/markdown-heavy replies (regression from #87896)

question: Is the current session-level report enough to promote a repair now, or should maintainers require live Feishu or trajectory proof showing where the long markdown final disappears before coding?
rationale: The user-visible regression is plausible and important, but source inspection does not yet identify whether the bug is in final extraction, Feishu delivery/card rendering, streaming close, or dispatch-count reconciliation.

options.title: Require live or trajectory proof first
options.body: Ask for a redacted Feishu transcript/log or run a live reproduction that shows assistant final content, delivery attempts, failed counts, and the fallback trigger before promoting a fix.

options.title: Allow a guarded source investigation
options.body: Permit a repair worker to add a regression harness only if it first reproduces the zero-final long-markdown path without broadly weakening fallback policy.

recommendation.title: Require live or trajectory proof first
recommendation.body: Ask for a redacted Feishu transcript/log or run a live reproduction that shows assistant final content, delivery attempts, failed counts, and the fallback trigger before promoting a fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent maintainer repair/comment history on the Feishu fallback PR makes steipete the best available owner for deciding proof sufficiency before another fallback change.
